extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking traditional publishers (especially those writing erotic, LGBTQ, BDSM, romance, or sexual-health nonfiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and practical submission guidance for authors who might query or submit manuscripts to Cleis Press, a publisher specializing in sexuality-related fiction and nonfiction. Includes current submission policy notes, subject/genre fit, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agented submissions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: They are currently open only to agented submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated October 9th 2023: Cleis is accepting submissions only from agents; the author notes uncertainty whether this is temporary or permanent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre/subject fit — primary focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Cleis Press ... focus on LGBTQ, BDSM, romance, and erotic writing for all sexual preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should target Cleis only if their work aligns with these central genres/themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction topic areas accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: They publish LGBTQ+ nonfiction as well as nonfiction on the topic of sex and sexuality, including self-help, sexual guides, LGBTQ+ and/or women’s studies, feminism, dating and relationships, sexual health, and memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonfiction submissions should match these topical areas; the page lists specific subcategories to determine fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erotic fiction acceptance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fictional work of an erotic nature is within their remit; pair this with the genre/subject-fit guidance above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow publisher's submission guidelines exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: They have detailed and specific submission guidelines that you must follow in order to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are directed to read and comply with Cleis's official guidelines (link provided on page) before submitting; failure to follow instructions may disqualify a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method — email only
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be made via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use other delivery methods; use the email process outlined in the publisher's guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and rejection assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have not heard from them 10 weeks after submitting, assume rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set expectations around response timeline—wait up to ~10 weeks before moving on or querying elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research current catalogue/releases to assess fit
rubrics_metrics.description: To get a feel for what they are releasing right now, go here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should review Cleis's recent/current titles to judge whether their manuscript matches the publisher's present list and editorial direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check publisher reputation and contract terms
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s clear Cleis has had serious issues in the past, and as of 2018, did not have an ideal contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to investigate publisher reputation and contract history (links provided) before signing; historical concerns over contracts are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher presentation varies (covers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Their covers run the gamut from good to genre appropriate, to amateurish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual presentation of titles varies — this may inform perceptions of market positioning and production values but is an observational note rather than an explicit submission requirement.
